title: Choose generic type parameters and constraints without replacing type safety with object casts

rubric.point: Constraint is the generic `IComparable<T>`, which supplies `CompareTo(T)` for both `int` and `string`

questions.model:
`IComparable<T>`

Optional: the non-generic `IComparable` takes an `object` argument, so it boxes an `int`. `INumber<T>` would exclude `string`.

rubric.point: Version A compiles, then fails at run time when the cast to `IHandler` executes (an `InvalidCastException` is thrown)
Version B is rejected at compile time because `AuditLog` does not satisfy the `IHandler` constraint, so the program does not build

questions.model:
- **A:** compiles. At run time the cast `(IHandler)handler` throws an `InvalidCastException`.
- **B:** compile-time error. `AuditLog` does not meet the `where T : IHandler` constraint, so the call is rejected before the code runs.
